sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:35

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:35:1
items.html:
And the whole aspect of AA is called the Keter of the entirety of all Atzilut: You must know that there are three general discernments in all the Partzufim of Atzilut: the first is the discernments of the roots of the Mochin; the second is the discernments of the Mochin themselves; the third is the discernment of ZON, who receive the Mochin. And this matter is required here by force of the upper Partzuf, which is SAG of AK, as known, since all the forces that exist in the upper one must be found in the one below it as well.
And you find there, at the beginning of the rooting of the partnership of the quality of mercy in judgment, that is, the ascent of the bottom Hey into the Einayim of SAG, which cast the AHP of all the degrees outside, that the Rosh of SAG of AK itself received this partnership into the ten Sefirot of its Rosh, and in it the beginning of this coupling of the bottom Hey in the Einayim came out. Even though it itself was in no way diminished from its degree because of this ascent, it nevertheless became a root for the discernment of this partnership, in which the discernment of the breaking of the degree was revealed in the secret of the hairs of the Dikna [beard]. Therefore, corresponding to it, two discernments of roots came out in Atzilut as well, called Atik and AA. The root of all the Mochin that come in the partnership of the quality of mercy in judgment is Atik, resembling the Rosh of SAG of AK, in which the coupling of the bottom Hey in the Einayim was made; and just as the matter of the AHP going outside could not yet be revealed in the Rosh of SAG itself, so this matter is not revealed in Atik either, but only in AA, which corresponds to the Dikna of SAG of AK, for everything made by force of the coupling in the Rosh of SAG is revealed only in its Dikna. So it is with AA and Atik as well: all the couplings made in Atik for the sake of the Mochin of Atzilut are not revealed in Atik itself, but only in AA, as this matter is written above, page 392, in the Inner Light, the passage beginning “And behold”. Study it there well. Thus the two Partzufim of Atik and AA have been explained, which are the discernment of the roots of the Mochin for Atzilut, similar to SAG of AK and its Dikna, which are the roots of the partnership of the bottom Hey in the Einayim.
And just as in SAG of AK, after the records, which are the discernment of Guf, were recognized, they descended to their place in the Guf, to the place of the Tabur of AK, and there the Mochin of the bottom Hey in the Einayim were revealed in the discernment of Rosh, so it is here in Atzilut too: after the coupling was made in AA and Atik upon the MAN [Mayin Nukvin] that rose for the sake of the Mochin, they descend to their place in the Guf, to the Chazeh [chest] of AA, for the revelation of the Mochin in their proper place, and these are called AVI of Atzilut, that is, the Mochin.
And by this you will understand the matter of the division of AVI of Atzilut into four discernments of AVI. You need only remember well everything that has been explained concerning the ascent of the screen that was refined from the Guf of SAG for the renewal of the coupling in the Rosh of SAG, until its arrival at the ZAT of Nekudim, brought in the two preceding parts.
Let us recall the matters briefly. The screen that rose from the Guf of SAG was included of three discernments of records: of the records of the tastes of SAG (see above, page 451, item 24), upon whose coupling the upper MA of SAG emerged, whose place, after the coupling, is discernible from the Peh of SAG up to above the Tabur of SAG. And since the tastes of SAG never descended below the Tabur and were not mixed at all with the inner NHY of AK, there is nothing in it of the bottom Hey, and it is reckoned as the upper AVI, as the ARI says above (page 396, item 6).
The second discernment of records is the records of the Nekudot of SAG, which are the nine lower ones of SAG that expanded from the Tabur downward to the Sium of the feet of AK, where they were mixed with the inner NHY of AK and were included of the bottom Hey. And upon their coupling the ten Sefirot of Nekudim emerged, out of the secret of the bottom Hey in the Einayim, which cast the AHP out of all the degrees. And after their coupling in the Rosh of SAG, their place is discernible at the Tabur of AK, and the first Rosh emerged from the Tabur upward to the Chazeh of SAG, which is the Peh of the upper MA mentioned above; and the GAR of Nekudim, in which there are two heads, Keter and AVI, whose place is from the Sium of Tifferet to the Tabur of AK.
And know that these three heads mentioned above, which emerged through the coupling upon the records of the Nekudot of SAG, are all called YESHSUT, and they are three discernments of YESHSUT. They are called so for the reason the ARI wrote above (page 397), that the discernments of SAG that are mixed with the inner MA and BON of AK are always called by the name YESHSUT, while those clean of this mixture are called by the name of the upper AVI. See there. And since these emerged upon the records of the discernments of the Nekudot of SAG, they are necessarily mixed with the bottom Hey of MA and BON of AK. Yet there are three degrees among them, for the first YESHSUT, which stands from the Tabur of AK upward, is the choicest of them all, because the bottom Hey serves in it from below upward, and it is known that coarseness cannot act in anything above the source of its being. Therefore this YESHSUT is reckoned as still clean of the bottom Hey, and is not even considered Nekudim, but is entirely similar to the discernment of the tastes of SAG, that is, to the upper AVI. Nevertheless it is certainly lower than they, since it does at least have the lights that come from the coupling of the bottom Hey, and it is at least considered a root for Nekudim, which is not so with the upper MA mentioned above, which is the discernment of the upper AVI, for they are not considered even a root for Nekudim, since they have nothing at all of those lights that bear any relation to the bottom Hey in the Einayim, as above.
The second degree is the second Rosh of Nekudim, which is called Keter. Since it is the discernments of the AHP of the first YESHSUT, the force of the bottom Hey already governs in it, and it is therefore considered a discernment of Nekudim. Yet since it too is itself divided, in its own ten Sefirot, into the discernment of Galgalta ve Einayim and AHP, which are two heads, Keter as well is regarded as one in which the bottom Hey serves from below upward, in the discernment of its Nikvey Einayim. Therefore the main governance of the bottom Hey in the Einayim is revealed chiefly in the third Rosh, which is called AVI of Nekudim. Thus the three degrees of YESHSUT have been explained: the first YESHSUT is almost entirely clean of the bottom Hey, and is considered a root of a root; the second YESHSUT, which is the Keter of Nekudim, is considered a root for the Mochin, which are AVI, in whom the bottom Hey governs, but it itself is still reckoned as having the bottom Hey below it; and the third YESHSUT, which is AVI of Nekudim, is considered the actual discernment of Nekudim, that is, the discernment of the bottom Hey in the Einayim, in whom this is revealed in its full governance.
Thus the two discernments of Atzilut have been explained. They are the roots of the Mochin of Atzilut, called Atik and AA, which correspond to the Rosh of SAG of AK and to its Dikna, where the coupling upon the screen was made only in the discernments of inclusion, for the sake of the lower one, and where, after the coarseness in the screen was recognized, it must descend to its place. In this same way the coupling was made in Atik and AA, that is, only in the discernments of inclusion, and this is called by the name of a root for the Mochin alone. And the second discernment has also been explained, which is AVI of Atzilut, who are the complete Mochin of Atzilut. But they are not the upper AVI, but only the fourth YESHSUT, corresponding to the fourth YESHSUT of SAG of AK, which is AVI of Nekudim, as above. And in this same way four discernments of AVI come out here too, and the fourth are the Mochin of Atzilut, meaning that they clothe in ZON of Atzilut, who are considered the receivers of the Mochin, for the whole matter of this partnership revolves upon them, since the conduct of the world is only from ZON, as known. However, although we have explained four discernments in AVI, they are nevertheless essentially reckoned as only two discernments, for the upper AVI are one discernment, and all three degrees of YESHSUT are likewise reckoned as one discernment.
And ZON of Atzilut, who are the receivers of the Mochin, correspond to the ZAT of Nekudim, which were born from the MAN of the Yesod of AK, which is called Shuruk. In Atzilut they divide into two discernments: the great ZON and the small ZON. This is because two discernments emerged in the ZAT of Nekudim, namely the four kings of DHGT from AVI, and the four kings TNHYM from YESHSUT. Therefore their like emerged in Atzilut as well, for the great ZON are ascribed to DHGT, and the small ZON are ascribed to TNHYM.
And this is what he says: “all these heads, one below the other, are all drawn together in the aspect of a single Partzuf that includes all of Atzilut in its entirety.” That is, as above, that all the Partzufim of Atzilut are revealed essentially only in ZON. For this renewal of the Mochin that was made in Atzilut, in the discernment of the partnership of the quality of mercy in judgment, since they must reveal the matter of the conduct of reward and punishment in this world, all of this belongs to ZON alone, for it is in them that this matter operates: at the time when the lower ones are worthy, they raise MAN and the Mochin are revealed in ZON, and at the time when they are not worthy, the Mochin depart. Above ZON, however, the actions of the lower ones cause no flaw at all. Thus the Mochin are essentially for the reception of ZON; but in order to bestow them upon ZON, they must cascade through the eight preceding Partzufim, which are Atik and his Nukva and AA and his Nukva, as the discernments of roots for the Mochin, and AVI and YESHSUT as the very discernments of the Mochin, for ZA cannot receive them except from the fourth YESHSUT, as above. And it turns out that they are all one Partzuf with one single function.
